extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comic-book writers and readers interested in Alan Moore's writing advice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing comic-book scripts and stories, covering idea generation, reader engagement (structure and pacing), worldbuilding, plotting, scripting details, and stylistic experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 1 – The Basic Idea: Thinking About Comics
rubrics_metrics.description: Focuses on the idea behind the whole work of art, and what the writer intends to express in his or her work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the core idea and the writer's intention as the foundation of the comic; think about what the work as a whole is meant to be or say before developing other elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 2 – Reaching The Reader: Structure, Pacing, Story Telling
rubrics_metrics.description: Examines what is going on in the reader's mind and gives tips on how to keep the reader focused on the comic book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structure and pacing deliberately to manage reader attention; consider reader cognition and craft storytelling choices (page turns, beats, rhythm) to maintain focus and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 3 – World Building: Place and Personality
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggests that writers examine real-life characters, people they know throughout their life, in order to create realistic fictional characters; gives hints about how to create a detailed universe, even if it means that the writer starts by creating economic structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground characters in observed real-life personalities for realism; build a detailed setting (including social/economic systems) to make the fictional world coherent and lived-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 4 – The Details: Plot and Script
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims to demolish the misunderstanding of the importance of plot. Moore delineates plot not as a list of things happening but more like a concept of time, contributing to the other elements of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think of plot as a temporal framework that interacts with character, theme and visual storytelling rather than merely a sequence of events; focus on how time and ordered events serve other artistic elements when scripting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Part – Afterwords (stylistic experimentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore advises writers 'never to get stuck in one writing style, always be open to try new things' and suggests established writers should 'simply try new and hard things they didn't think they could manage'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid stylistic complacency; deliberately experiment with new forms, techniques and challenges to grow as a writer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall beginner's guidance: writing, storytelling and plotting a comic book script
rubrics_metrics.description: The first four chapters function as a beginner's guide about writing, storytelling and plotting a comic book script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For newcomers, prioritize mastering idea generation, reader-focused structure and pacing, believable worldbuilding, and understanding plot as temporal and integrative; use the book's chapters as a course-like progression through these fundamentals.
